children: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has formally ordered Tesla

to answer a series of detailed questions by September 30 whether the design of the Cybercab—specifically the lack of a steering wheel and brake/gas pedals—might conflict with federal safety standards.
Regulators want to know if Tesla
had initially designed the vehicle in some way that can be driven by a human or if controls can be temporarily installed, a feature that may have led Tesla
to certify the vehicle as compliant with federal motor vehicle safety standards (FMVSS).

“State whether temporarily installed human driver controls or other equipment for use by a human driver were a part of Tesla’s basis for certifying compliance with any FMVSS,” NHTSA said in the order.

is a two-seater vehicle made specifically for ridesharing. Without mirrors, a steering wheel, gas or brake pedals, the car is completely autonomous while also designed to meet all applicable rules to operate on public roads.
does not respond to NHTSA’s Special Order, the company can be referred to the Department of Justice for a civil action to compel a response with potentially penalties up to $27,874 per day.
If the vehicle is determined to be non-compliant, NHTSA can order a full recall of all Cybercabs.

wants the Cybercab to be fully autonomous without any human intervention, it can modify the vehicle to meet NHTSA standards with a removable steering wheel, brake, and gas pedals using the vehicle's wire system that enables steering and braking.
Under current federal law, fully self-driving vehicles do not need NHTSA approval if they have steering wheels, brake pedals, mirrors, and other features that enable human control.
